components/StatementAnalysis.tsx: Agent-managed rent arrives net: management fees, letting fees, water and repairs come out before the disbursement, so this sits below the lease rent by design.
As many as you like. Nothing already loaded is replaced.
Cash in and cash out above the threshold, because both raise a question — one about where money is going, the other about where it came from.
Changes how other people’s statements are read — removable in Settings.
Closing balance across the accounts, month by month.
Conduct is read before income. One overdrawn day is usually forgivable; a pattern of dipping under before payday says the household is running on empty whatever the income figure says.
Credits carrying the client’s own name
Declared as part of gross but not paid inside this window
Deducted before the credit lands, so the credits look smaller than the salary
Detected by provider name, then grouped so you can see which services are in use rather than one lump sum.
Drop another workbook here, or click to choose
Every cash deposit has a withdrawal of similar size behind it.
Every credit matched to an employer, grouped by payer. Only money arriving on a regular cycle is counted — an irregular pattern is not safe to annualise.
Every day of the period walked, with the closing balance on each account.
Every repeating debit that looks like credit. Living expenses are excluded — this is credit only.
Every transaction on the day the balance bottomed out.
Everything credited that is not salary or rent, grouped by payer. Only money that repeats is counted as income.
Extra super, a novated lease or a packaged car never appears in the account
Genuine savings is not the balance — it is the part that has stayed put. The test takes the lowest the combined balance reached.
Government payments, grouped by benefit rather than lumped together.

It assumes a resident with no HELP debt, no salary sacrifice and no other deduction taken before the money lands. Any of those means the real gross is HIGHER than this — the gross-up can only understate, never overstate. It is never written to the fact find.

It is not a figure to type into a servicing calculator. Family payments generally need a current Centrelink income statement and are often only counted while the children are under a set age; child support needs its own evidence. Treat this as a prompt to go and get it.

Matching to the fact find is by lender name, not by amount, so a loan debiting more than declared still counts as declared. A single debit to a lender is a one-off payment until it happens twice, and is listed rather than counted.
Most lenders read the trend and the share of income rather than the total. Rising month on month, or above roughly five per cent of credits, is where it starts costing the deal.
Nothing disagrees and every credit is accounted for.
Nothing is changed automatically. The fact find still says what it said. This card exists so the file carries the question and your answer to it before an assessor asks the same thing.

One credit in the period says nothing about a year, so single credits are listed separately and never multiplied up. Money between the client’s own accounts, credits carrying their own name, and refunds or rebates are all set aside rather than counted — each is shown here so you can disagree.
Part of the pay is split somewhere we were not given

Re-run servicing before the conversation rather than after — and net it against any income found above, which may more than cover it. Buy now pay later is the most common miss, because clients very often do not think of it as credit at all.
Read it as an indication, not a decision. Lenders define genuine savings differently: some accept rent paid instead, some count shares or term deposits, some want a percentage of purchase price.

Read the benefit type, not just the amount. Family Tax Benefit is widely accepted and often shaded; child support usually needs the assessment or court order; JobSeeker and most allowances are not accepted at all.
Recurring credit obligations debiting the accounts that do not appear on the fact find.
Recurring income being credited that is not on the fact find. Unlike an undisclosed liability, this one is usually in the client’s favour.
Rent going out, matched to an agent and checked against the day of the month.
Rental credits, grouped by who paid them.
Returned items with the fee that came with them. A fee and its item on the same day are one event.
Showing the most recent set on its own.
Stability is what carries a casual or contract client and what sinks one. The test is whether pay arrives on a predictable cycle, from the same payer, in a steady amount.

The direction matters more than the amount. Accumulation per month is the client’s demonstrated surplus — if the proposed repayment sits well above it, raise that before an assessor does.

The monthly figure is the total over the period scaled to a month, not the size of one pay. If the period does not hold a whole number of cycles the two differ slightly, and the total is the honest one.
The provider list is a setting, not something buried in code. New names get added as they turn up.
